confirmed_blocking.summary: After the R2-Q2 post-commit cleanup failure, the prescribed recovery `resume <branch>` exits 3 'matches several runs': the kept pending file <repo>-adopt-<branch>.json matches the same name as the new worktree run, so the protected contract's only recovery fails.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: Judge reproduction in a scratch copy of HEAD: `adopt 007-x` -> exit 1 'committed 23fed23; pending cleanup failed: resume 007-x, do not retry'; then `resume 007-x` -> exit 3 "'007-x' matches several runs: .../repo-factory/007-x/specs/007-x/factory/state.json, .../home/pending/repo-adopt-007-x.json". find_matches (commands.py:243-256) matches the pending run through name_matches ('repo-adopt-007-x' ends with '-007-x'), and deduped (221-235) keys pending and worktree copies apart, so one_run (283-284) exits 3. A retry refuses on the existing factory/state.json and points back to resume, so the user must delete the pending file by hand. No test runs resume after the cleanup failure.
confirmed_blocking.fix: In find_matches (or one_run), when a pending match's name is <repo-name>-adopt-<branch> and a worktree match for the same branch in the same repo exists, drop the pending match so `resume <branch>` resolves to the worktree run. Add a regression test on `bin/factory resume <run>`: after the cleanup-failure fault, `resume 007-x` exits 0 and names the worktree run. Keep the protected message wording. Consider fixing R3-STD-3's lock release in the same change.
